RESEARCH_REPORT/v1

Date: 2026-09-11
Research substrate: ordinary Chat/web research, not Codex execution.
Purpose: resolve current Google/Gemini auth assumptions before runner engineering.

Findings from current official Google documentation:

1. Gemini API's minimum/default developer path is API-key authentication. Current API reference requires `x-goog-api-key`; Google AI Studio creates/manages Gemini API keys.
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/api ; https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/get-started

2. New API keys created in Google AI Studio are now **Auth keys**, tied to a Google Cloud project. Google is retiring/rejecting unrestricted legacy Standard keys in September 2026; do not design new infrastructure around an unrestricted Standard key.
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key (last updated 2026-09-02 UTC at research time)

3. A Gemini/AI Studio project can remain on **Free Tier without a linked Cloud Billing account**. Moving to paid Tier 1 requires explicit billing setup; current docs describe linking billing/prepay as the paid upgrade action. Therefore a fail-closed `free_only` provider guard is architecturally meaningful.
   Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/modify-project

4. OAuth is supported when stricter access controls are required, but Google's own Gemini OAuth quickstart states API key is the easiest/default method. OAuth should therefore be treated as a possible later hardening/enterprise path, not a prerequisite for the smallest Free Tier runner.
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/oauth

5. Keys inherit project/billing context; they are not an independent billing boundary. The runner should therefore reason about a provider capability tied to known project/tier metadata, not merely possession of a key string.
   Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing

Engineering implication:
`provider capability = credential handle + project/tier policy + privacy class + free_only guard + revocation metadata`, with the reusable secret kept outside worker/model context.

This research resolves documentation uncertainty only. It does not authorize creation of a Google project/key, billing, or secret disclosure. Successor implementation: #112 RUNNER-FREE-INFERENCE-0003.
